name: Pre-Earnings Momentum
summary: A fixed pre-earnings stock-selection study with a failed primary portfolio endpoint and a separately labeled exploratory cash-sweep replay.

variations.name: Pre-Earnings Momentum — Study 1
variations.thesis: Stocks meeting the frozen pre-earnings momentum selection rules would outperform SPY in the one-shot holdout portfolio test.

methodology.summary: A frozen no-cash-sweep portfolio simulation evaluated the pre-registered holdout after development and embargo periods.
methodology.population: Eligible liquid stocks with upcoming earnings events and the required current strategy signals.
inclusionCriteria: Upcoming earnings two through five weeks away.
Super High or High eligible signal band with the frozen liquidity and freshness rules.
exclusionCriteria: Stocks outside the fixed price, liquidity, event, sector, or position constraints.
features: Frozen momentum signal and liquidity gates.
Weekly Friday decisions with fixed portfolio allocation rules.
methodology.endpoint: Holdout portfolio return relative to SPY; daily excess versus SPY is reported with a 95% interval.
controls: SPY buy-and-hold over the identical holdout window.
Frozen random eligible controls recorded in the historical run.
methodology.inference: The primary portfolio comparison is frozen. The daily-excess interval is descriptive and does not rescue a failed portfolio endpoint.
limitations: The observed holdout is spent and cannot be reused for validation.
Cash exposure makes the portfolio comparison different from fully invested SPY.

outcome.summary: The frozen primary portfolio returned +22.42% versus SPY +49.17% across 281 completed trades, so the primary endpoint failed.
whatWorked: The fixed pipeline produced the planned holdout and completed trades.
whatDidNotWork: Mean daily excess versus SPY had a 95% interval crossing zero.
nextSteps: Keep the failed primary result visible.
Do not treat current candidates as evidence of a validated edge.

moreData.rationale: The pre-specified holdout is spent; more observations cannot convert it into a fresh validation test.

scan.eligibilityExplanation: The operational scan applies the current pre-earnings candidate selection rules, not a new historical test.
scan.warning: This scan reproduces the studied selection rules; the historical primary endpoint failed, so candidates are not evidence of a validated edge.

caveats: The failed primary portfolio endpoint remains the study verdict.
Current candidates are operational matches, not historical candidate rows or validated recommendations.

variations.name: SPY Cash Sweep — Study 2
variations.thesis: Mechanically sweeping idle portfolio cash into SPY could remove the deployment gap observed in Study 1, but this replay is exploratory because both the dates and sweep followed Study 1.

methodology.summary: The inherited selection pipeline was replayed on the already-spent Study 1 dates with a fixed SPY cash sweep.
methodology.endpoint: Exploratory spent-window portfolio comparison and daily excess versus SPY; neither has validation weight.
controls: SPY buy-and-hold over the identical spent window.
The inherited fixed selection pipeline with the mechanical SPY sweep.
methodology.period: Exploratory spent-window replay of decisions 2025-04-04 through 2026-06-26.
methodology.inference: All results are descriptive only. The window was observed by Study 1 and the sweep was designed afterward.
limitations: The dates and sweep behavior were selected after Study 1.
This replay cannot validate the strategy or support an edge claim.

outcome.summary: The exploratory spent-window replay returned +53.16% versus SPY +49.17%, but it has no validation weight because it followed Study 1.
whatWorked: The fully invested sweep replay exceeded SPY over the already-spent window.
whatDidNotWork: The post-outcome design and spent dates prevent a confirmatory verdict.
nextSteps: Retain the result as exploratory evidence only.
A prospective or PIT-historical holdout would require a dated amendment.

moreData.rationale: Only a separately pre-specified prospective or PIT-historical evaluation could provide fresh validation evidence.

caveats: This is an exploratory replay on dates already spent by Study 1.
The cash-sweep variation does not alter the failed Study 1 primary verdict.
